title: An early report with Isaiah’s motifs woven in

phrase.meaning: recite in the name of your Lord

points.label: A remembered event
points.text: In the tradition, **Aisha** tells the story, passed on by her nephew ʿUrwa and by al-Zuhri; al-Bukhari places it near the start of his Sahih. The shock and the reply “I am not a reciter” are read as the Prophet’s own memory.

points.label: Early, but shaped
points.text: **Görke and Schoeler** trace the iqraʾ story through al-Zuhri back to **ʿUrwa** (d. 712). Yet they call it “possible, or even probable” that motifs from **Isaiah 40:6** helped shape it.

points.label: A later literary scene
points.text: **Stephen Shoemaker** suggests al-Zuhri himself built the long version from a shorter report. **Paul Neuenkirchen** reads the scene as based on Isaiah 40:6: how later Muslims imagined their prophet, not a record of the event.

bottom_text: No consensus. The evidence leans to a story circulating by about 700 with biblical call motifs in it; whether a real experience lies beneath cannot be tested from these sources.
source_label: Görke, Motzki & Schoeler, “First Century Sources for the Life of Muhammad?” (2012)
